orchestration.guarantee: Work, actors and configured policies preserve owner intent, validation and application composition through injected ports; effect failures retain safe public diagnostics and known outcomes without repeating effects.

storage.guarantee: Replaceable stores pass the xcontracts StateStore conformance kit and the SQLite store keeps its persistence behavior.

versioning.guarantee: Configuration and durable state declare format versions; unsupported versions are refused with explicit codes, structural validation constructs nothing, and nothing is rewritten or migrated on load.

release.guarantee: A release tag, the package version, the xork alias version and its exact pin, and the changelog agree before publishing, and both distributions are built, accepted and published together; the launcher, under either command name, reports how it or its alias was installed and the matching upgrade command; the install script provides uv and installs the launcher without elevated privileges.

capabilities.guarantee: Configured capability providers and evaluators preserve discovery, invocation, permissions and assessment evidence across process adapters; PR reads honor their configured repository scope before hosting access.

delivery.guarantee: Queued messages, delivery attempts, retries and recovery preserve recipient scope, effect uncertainty and causal receipts; default session selection follows witnessed creation order independently of UTC labels, with explicit legacy fallback.

sessions.guarantee: Session adapters preserve native conversations, resume, concurrent progress and turn ownership through their declared protocols.

bridge.guarantee: External session attachment and callbacks preserve connection leases, operation ownership and cleanup across process transports.

identity.guarantee: Independent evidence joins reject stale, contradictory or missing caller/session identity across interchangeable decoders and product receipts.

work-acceptance.guarantee: Completion and assessment require current, correctly bound evidence without losing owner goals or conflating turn completion with accepted work.

state.guarantee: Configurable state definitions and shared transition enforcement preserve guards, versions, history and lifecycle integration.

transport.guarantee: Transport boundaries preserve framing, autonomous progress, cancellation, limits and cleanup while exposing explicit failures.

project-server.guarantee: One long-running server shares an application across client connections: the same MCP session over every client transport, per-connection actors, server-wide admission, owner-only peers, a single auto-started instance, sessions that outlive their client and a draining stop.

terminal-host.guarantee: Every terminal host adapter and the memory fake keep one behaviour: named terminals with exact environments, known exit status or signal, bounded output and logs that outlive the terminal, identity-fenced control, adoption only by verified receipt and survival of a killed controller where the host claims it.

projects.guarantee: Nothing runs without a set-up project. A project is identified on a machine by its git common directory, so every worktree shares one instance and one server and a separate clone is refused; only an approved tracked configuration renders or runs; the user's overlay wins over the project, guardrails included; worktree identity reaches records, events, telemetry and guardrails; and the release a project pins runs its commands.

upgrade.guarantee: An instance moves to a newly pinned release only through an explicit upgrade of an approved pin: the server is stopped (refused while sessions are live unless detached), the corpus is snapshotted and the state backed up before the target release checks and migrates the data, the new release is recorded only after it reads the configuration, data and telemetry, and a failed or interrupted upgrade leaves the old release recorded and resumes on the next run.

verification.guarantee: Independent checker observations, verdicts and fault attribution establish the selected candidate behavior without using product verdicts as the oracle.

architecture.guarantee: Deterministic dependency policy and planted violations preserve product, test-kit, scenario and evidence-decoder boundaries. Event advice distinguishes verified source identity from protected inference evidence and authorizes refetched review identities before provider use.

live-acceptance.guarantee: The public-process MCP scenario retains native callback and persistence evidence and proves cleanup of owned terminal resources.

framework.guarantee: Shared execution, resource ownership, configuration, evidence and collection guarantee complete declared plans and honest outcomes for every selected test family.

telemetry.guarantee: Telemetry capture, queries, preservation and optional export retain scoped evidence, gaps and original action outcomes; the in-tree collector keeps immutable, integrity-checked corpus and artifact storage behind selected adapters and reads existing corpora and bundles.

contracts.guarantee: The public ports, their values and errors and the adapter factory convention come from xcontracts unchanged; built-in adapters are selectable through that convention and satisfy its ports and conformance kit, and xcontracts depends on nothing but the standard library.

agent-guidance.guarantee: Shared agent skills have one source that every harness location mirrors by relative symlink, front matter a strict YAML reader accepts, guidance pointers and section anchors that resolve, and no local paths, session identifiers or foreign emails in the skills, the workflow guidance or the Serena project; the importing instruction file loads the repository rules, whose agent workflow section points at the skills; the Serena project selects the python language server and the tools interface, honours .gitignore, ships Serena's own .gitignore and ignores its cache, memories and local overrides.
